_meta.purpose: Defines packaging as a tenant/RBAC entitlement view over flattened microservices and clean-architecture layers. Market labels are not product, module, service, crate, or ownership boundaries.

directives.rule: Every implementation artifact remains a flattened microservice or layer-specific clean-architecture crate: domain, application, API, runtime, infrastructure, kernel, or library support as appropriate.
Packaging decisions are computed from tenant entitlements, RBAC roles, policy scopes, regulatory packs, residency, and feature flags.
A package must never grant access directly; it resolves to RBAC scopes evaluated by the owning microservice and tenant policy plane.
Messenger, community, and mail are concrete services; no communications wrapper or product grouping exists above them.

target_users.authorization: tenant owner or delegated admin RBAC role
microservice role binding plus tenant entitlement
compliance RBAC role scoped by regulatory pack

acceptance_criteria.given: a tenant has package entitlements and RBAC bindings
acceptance_criteria.when: a user requests a microservice surface
acceptance_criteria.then: the package resolves to tenant-scoped RBAC roles and policy scopes; the owning microservice still performs the authorization decision

acceptance_criteria.given: a market label such as communications, broad business operations, or regulated care is used in GTM copy
acceptance_criteria.then: no product/module/service/crate boundary is created from that market label; concrete services stay flattened and independently owned
